FN-DIKKNHN-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 247
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility & Economic Sponsor: Senator Steve Livingston
Development
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/03/2024
Senate Bill 247 as introduced would rename the existing Alabama Department of Labor as the
Alabama Department of Workforce (ADOW) and designate the head of the department as the
Secretary of Workforce. This bill would also restructure the ADOW, and increase its'
administrative and financial obligations by an undetermined amount by expanding the general
functions and duties of the ADOW to include: (1) serving as the centralized data and
information repository for the workforce development activities of the state; and (2)
administering and overseeing certain state and federal workforce development programs and
entities currently administered and overseen by the Department of Commerce (DOC).
Additionally, this bill would: (1) transfer to the newly restructured department from DOC all
state-owned assets and state-level staff currently assigned to regional workforce councils; (2)
require current appointed division chiefs, currently subject to the State Merit System, to serve in
the exempt service; and (3) allow members of the Alabama Workforce Board, members of its'
executive committee, and members of the regional workforce boards to be reimbursed for
reasonable expenses incurred in the performance of the duties of the office.

FN-DIKKNHN-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 247
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility Sponsor: Senator Steve Livingston
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/15/2024
Senate Bill 247 as passed the Senate would rename the existing Alabama Department of Labor
as the Alabama Department of Workforce (ADOW) and designate the head of the department as
the Secretary of Workforce. This bill would also restructure the ADOW, and increase its'
administrative and financial obligations by an undetermined amount by expanding the general
functions and duties of the ADOW to include: (1) serving as the centralized data and
information repository for the workforce development activities of the state; and (2)
administering and overseeing certain state and federal workforce development programs and
entities currently administered and overseen by the Department of Commerce (DOC).
Additionally, this bill would: (1) transfer to the newly restructured department from DOC all
state-owned assets and state-level staff currently assigned to regional workforce councils; (2)
provide for three additional exempt employees of the department, whose compensation shall be
set by the Secretary; (3) provide for the employment of a division chief of the Workforce
Pathway Division; (4) repeal provisions regarding the directors of unemployment compensation
and employment services; and (5) allow members of the Alabama Workforce Board, members
of its' executive committee, and members of the regional workforce boards to be reimbursed for
reasonable expenses incurred in the performance of the duties of the office.
